title: Contributing
description: How the repository is laid out, how work is split, how to test a change, and how this site is built from the repository's Markdown.
hast: The repository is one checkout: the toolkit, its widget set, the applications, the distribution and this site. The code is on
the toolkit: display protocols, rasterizer, layout, text, the class parser
the widget set, Odin translations of the shadcn/ui components
the suite that diffs those widgets against Chromium rendering the React source
the applications, the window manager and
the four examples and the headless test suite
the distribution: kernel, init, login, palm, the installer, recipes, images
design documents and the screenshots the README shows
what is not done, in the order it is worth doing
Most of this repository was built by several agents working at once, each owning one directory. The rules they follow are written once, at the top of
, so that any prompt there can be handed over without more context. They are worth following by hand too:

Every prompt below assumes the conventions this project already runs on. Rather
than repeat them in each one, they are here once, and each prompt says which
apply.
The standing rules, which belong in every prompt:

are off limits unless the task is about them, and
that other agents are working in other directories concurrently. If a build
fails inside shared code, that is somebody else mid-edit: wait and retry,
never "fix" it.
Work in a git worktree when the task touches

, not a build: several agents editing
the toolkit in one tree each see the others' regressions with no way to tell
them apart. Worktrees make every parity run trustworthy, and the merge is
cheap if the file ownership is disjoint — decide that up front and say it.
Never end a tool call with shared code uncompilable.

Several real bugs have passed every assertion and been visibly wrong — a
selection that flashed an entire line grey, a shadow measured faster and
drawn differently, a border colour silently falling back to its default.

, which runs on a private
invisible compositor — no lock, no queue, nothing on the user's screen.

The session scratchpad is shared between
agents: one had its harness script overwritten mid-run by another's copy
pointing at a different tree, and another's sweep iterated over a neighbour's
binaries and briefly opened windows on the user's screen.

The safety rules, which are not negotiable and must be restated in full in
any prompt they touch:

. Nothing may disable the radio or drop a

off the network.

Never read the user's real credential stores, mail, or financial files.
needs a password on this machine.

An agent cannot be given one and
must never cache, embed or prompt for one. Anything needing root stops at the
line and says what a person has to run.

A claim in a document should come from running the command next to it.
explains why: one session found five of its claims false at once.
The site is a React Router app in

lists every synced page and the file, or the section of a file, it comes from. To publish a new document, add it there; to change what a page says, change the source document, not the site.
